title: Standardize build entrypoints to Go runner and prune dev dependencies
author: Aisha K. Patel
release_notes: Replaced ad-hoc shell/curl build entrypoints with a small Go-based build runner for hermetic local dev and CI; removed unused dev dependencies and trimmed Docker build layers. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context: over the last year the repo accumulated multiple ad-hoc shell entrypoints (scripts/bootstrap.sh, ci/run-steps.sh, docker/entrypoint.sh) used by local dev, CI, and release automation. These scripts are hard to cache, fragile across platforms, and make the CI matrix rely on varying shell behavior. This PR standardizes build entrypoints on a tiny Go runner binary (cmd/buildrunner) that: 1) exposes a typed CLI for common steps (install-deps, build, test, package), 2) performs deterministic dependency pruning (devonly removal) for Docker/CI artifacts, and 3) emits structured logs and exit codes the CI can consume. Motivation: improve hermeticity, speed up CI by enabling consistent layer caching, and reduce surface area of devDependencies across SDKs. Changes are split into several logical commits and include CI workflow updates and documentation in dev/README.

Checklist: - [x] Introduce cmd/buildrunner Go binary with subcommands for install/build/test/package - [x] Replace shell entrypoints referenced by ci/workflows/* and Dockerfiles - [x] Add dep-prune step (node/yarn and python venv) used before packaging images - [x] Remove unused dev dependencies from package.json and pyproject.toml where safe - [x] Update CI workflows to call buildrunner and consume structured logs - [x] Add smoke CI job (ci/smoke-fast.yml) that exercises new runner - [x] Add docs/dev-build.md with migration guidance - [ ] Monitor CI for 48h post-merge (follow-up ticket ENG-2030)

Context notes: Linear ENG-2027 tracks the build runner work; SUP-773 was a customer support ticket where inconsistent build artifacts caused bad images in a Dedicated install. This PR is intentionally conservative with pruning rules (only removes devDependencies that are not referenced in runtime bundles per static analysis). For Python packages we pin wheel build path and remove test-only extras before packaging.
commits:
1) feat(buildrunner): add initial Go CLI and install/build/test subcommands (cmd/buildrunner/*)
2) ci: replace shell entrypoints in ci/workflows with buildrunner invocations; add smoke-fast.yml
3) infra: update Dockerfiles to use buildrunner artifact; add dep-prune scripts and manifest changes
4) deps: remove dev-only packages from package.json and tox.ini after static analysis
5) docs: add dev-build.md and update CONTRIBUTING.md
review_thread:
Diego Mendez: Can we guarantee the Go runner produces identical exit codes and log format as the replaced shell scripts?
Aisha: The runner intentionally maps to the same exit codes; added unit tests for mapping behavior and an adapter for previous log prefixes. See cmd/buildrunner/runner_test.go.
Lina Zhou: Removing these dev deps looks risky for some SDK examples — did you run the sample apps smoke tests?
Aisha: Yes — smoke-fast CI runs the JS/TS SDK sample apps and passes in this branch; also ran local samples against a dedicated docker image. I left a few borderline packages in package.json but marked them with a comment for follow-up.
Ravi Kapoor: CI speed improvement numbers?
Aisha: Measured wall-clock on main vs branch on the nightly matrix: average reduction of 17% in build+test lanes (cold start) and 9% on warm caches. Logs included in the PR artifacts.
Diego (request changes): Please add a short migration note for infra teams that use custom base images (we can't assume buildrunner is present).
Aisha: Added docs/dev-build.md and a Dockerfile snippet showing how to install the runner into custom base images.
Lina: Approving pending CI green.
Ravi: Approving.
Maintainer bot: all checks passed; auto-merge scheduled.

Final status: pass.
